name: 32019-sharegptlora-gptoss20b-1gpu
model: openai/gpt-oss-20b, served with the LoRA adapter jeeejeee/gpt-oss-20b-lora-adapter-text2sql (r=8, lora_alpha=32) attached to every request
hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of an a3 node (--gres=gpu:1), sm90.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, no expert parallelism, one vLLM engine, no router and no external cache tier.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=16, warmup the first 2%, no cooldown, bounded at 1000 requests with an 1800 s safety cap, seed static 32019.
workload: synthetic_text, single turn, no prefix_buckets, prompts of exactly 227 tokens and outputs of exactly 300 (min = max on both sides). Greedy at temperature 0.0, EOS ignored, posted plain to /v1/completions; prompts share no prefix and prefix caching is off. Every request is routed through the adapter named in scenario.json backend.lora_modules. Prompts are tokenized with add_special_tokens=True, so the engine counts a few tokens more than 227.
purpose: A text-to-SQL assistant on a 20-billion-parameter model with a LoRA adapter, serving 16 concurrent single-turn requests on one GPU.
launch:
# The serve command for this workload. Nothing here is tuned; there is no tuned.yaml and no
# tunable.yaml. The engine is the source checkout named by `configs/env.yaml: venv`.

model: openai/gpt-oss-20b
tensor-parallel-size: 1
max-num-seqs: 16

# The adapter itself is named request-side in `scenario.json: backend.lora_modules` -- this
# launch path builds the engine directly and has no `--lora-modules` server flag.
enable-lora: true
max-loras: 1
max-lora-rank: 8

enable-prefix-caching: false
compilation-config: {"compile_sizes": [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]}

# PINNED, and load-bearing. Do not delete it as "the default": the library default is smaller
# than what a real `vllm serve` resolves to on this card, and the difference is a scheduling
# difference in how a 16-prompt batch is prefilled.
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

max-model-len: 4096
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
